doc.title: Harold Danko interviewed by Monk Rowe, via Zoom, April 28, 2021

title: Studying with Dolores Spitzer and the trouble reading ear-blind
summary: A teacher at 16 discovers he does not read but figures music out; he has to know how it sounds or functions.

story.theme_name: Growing up and learning music: family, first instruments, teachers
story.community_name: Reading music versus faking and playing by ear

blocks.x: Absolutely, yeah, yeah. It’s really one of those things where I’m really glad I had that — I wish I had been a little more disciplined about reading because it was one of those things where I tried to hear it and I talked about — I was explaining once about I could never be ear-blind. There was a teacher when I was about 16 I went to study with a wonderful teacher named Dolores Spitzer who had me sight read something that was on the piano. And after a couple of bars she said, “You don’t read, do you?” And she said, “You try to figure it out.” And I said that’s exactly right, you know like and she said, “You’ve got to just read the next note like the paper, like you’re reading.” And I just like had this concept, I just can’t do it ear-blind. I’ve got to know kind of what it sounds like or how does it function you know. And so as I went along I could kind of sight read Mozart, I could kind of sight read Scott Joplin. But the music that I really like is very dissonant and so I really had a problem reading stuff that was, you know I had to analyze it first.
